Hi Ava — looping in a short read of our commercial/legal stance so Procurement has a baseline before legal reviews. See attached redwood_clauses_summary.pdf for clause crosswalks. Key points: 

1) IP / model training: Redwood will not assert ownership of Customer Data or Customer Models. We grant Pioneer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to outputs for internal business use. We cannot provide a license for outputs to be used for retraining Redwood public models. For customers who require training rights, we offer a separate, priced addendum (Dedicated Private offering).

2) Liability cap: Our standard is higher of (12 months of fees) or $1M for proof-of-concept/short pilots; for enterprise commitments we propose a tiered approach – 1x annual spend for standard commercial, 2x annual spend for uptime-critical (SLA-backed) services, capped at $5M absolute. We will consider higher caps with an associated commitment/overage/insurance.

3) Indemnity: We accept indemnity for IP infringement for software delivered by Redwood, subject to standard procedures (notice, control of defense, mitigation). We cannot accept open-ended indemnity for regulatory fines (customer-caused data misuse). We propose a carve-out for claims arising from Customer's modification of the service or misuse.

4) Escrow / on-prem: We support escrow for on-prem/dedicated installs; typical triggers are vendor insolvency and extended breach of support obligations. We use third-party agent EscrowCorp and can share standard language. Escrow does not include ongoing operational runbooks unless requested in SOW.

- Pioneer: confirm whether they will accept a tiered liability cap; indicate any insurance thresholds.
- Legal: Jonas / Mina, please review redwood_clauses_summary and advise on any mandatory edits.

Subject: Final Q&A and recommended language for Pioneer — IP, indemnity, caps, escrow

Ava / Samir / Pioneer team,

Thanks for the thoughtful notes. Below are our consolidated answers and recommended contract language. We attached a clean PDF (redwood_final_qna_20261107.pdf) with clause snippets that legal can copy into your draft. Highlights follow — please treat this as Redwood's legal position for the current negotiation round: 

1) IP & Outputs
- Customer Data: Pioneer retains ownership of Customer Data. Redwood receives a limited license to process Customer Data to provide the Service.
- Service Output: Redwood grants Pioneer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to Service Outputs for internal business use. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Service Outputs to train Redwood's public models without explicit, written opt-in. For customers that require training rights, we offer a separately priced Training Addendum for Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) Indemnity
- Redwood will indemnify Pioneer for third-party claims that the service, as provided, infringes third-party IP, subject to standard notice and control provisions. Redwood's indemnity obligations exclude claims arising from Pioneer modifications, combination with third-party products, or Customer Data content.
- Redwood cannot indemnify for regulatory fines or penalties stemming from Customer's misuse of data; appropriate cooperation and notice obligations are required.

3) Liability Cap
- Proposed default: higher of 12 months of fees or $1,000,000 for standard commercial engagements.
- For SLA-backed, enterprise critical services (defined in Exhibit A), liability increases to the higher of 24 months of fees or $5,000,000.
- We agree to consider higher caps tied to explicit commitments (multi-year purchase, increased security attestations, or evidence of insurance).

4) Escrow / On-prem
- Redwood supports source-code escrow for Dedicated/on-prem deliveries. Standard trigger events: (i) Redwood insolvency; (ii) Redwood breach of support obligations for 90 days; or (iii) prolonged failure to meet SLA (per Exhibit B).
- Escrow materials include source necessary to restart and maintain deployed services but exclude internal operational runbooks unless explicitly purchased in SOW. We recommend using EscrowCorp as the agent and shared escrow agreement language (included).

5) Misc / Order Form
- Order form templates will enumerate committed capacity tiers, billing cadence, and overage pricing. Any changes to committed capacity that cross a pricing tier require 30 days' notice.

Next steps:
- Pioneer: confirm whether the tiered liability approach is acceptable or propose a counter with supporting insurance numbers.
- Pioneer legal (Samir): if you prefer a redline vs call, please provide a tracked draft; otherwise propose two 45-minute windows next week for a joint legal call.

Attachments: redwood_final_qna_20261107.pdf

Regards,
